But still i have now opened a room, and its  blank with this log: [TimelineDebug][!iSEWGSeKXHsiLbLrTR:matrix.org] diffs=[Reset] items 0->0
I would like that there is at least 20 events every time. Check the cache logic in the core, here is also element x logic for cache:
There are two places where the SQLite store is wired up — both pass dataPath and cachePath directly to the Rust ClientBuilder.sqliteStore():

1. First login — AuthenticationClientFactory.swift:38

ClientBuilder
    .sqliteStore(config: .init(dataPath: sessionDirectories.dataPath,
                               cachePath: sessionDirectories.cachePath)
        .passphrase(passphrase: passphrase))
Fresh SessionDirectories are created (new UUID), stored into a RestorationToken, and that token is saved to Keychain.

2. Subsequent launches / session restore — UserSessionStore.swift:141

ClientBuilder
    .sqliteStore(config: .init(dataPath: credentials.restorationToken.sessionDirectories.dataPath,
                               cachePath: credentials.restorationToken.sessionDirectories.cachePath)
        .passphrase(passphrase: credentials.restorationToken.passphrase))
The same UUID paths are read back from the RestorationToken in Keychain, so the Rust SDK opens the existing SQLite files.

The full chain

App launch
  → KeychainController reads RestorationToken
    → SessionDirectories { dataPath, cachePath } (same UUIDs as first login)
      → UserSessionStore restores client
        → ClientBuilder.sqliteStore(dataPath:cachePath:passphrase:)
          → Rust SDK opens existing SQLite DB
            → Timeline diffs delivered immediately on subscribeForUpdates()
The "cache logic" is entirely delegated to the Rust SDK — Element X just hands it the two directory paths and a passphrase. The SDK manages what goes in dataPath (persistent, encrypted: event store, crypto) vs cachePath (evictable: media, room lists).
